passages.heading: Summary
passages.text: This note details the setup and execution of the DQN agent for Ms. Pac-Man for Assignment 2. The main result is a comparison between two training runs, showing that rerunning the notebook with 450 games yielded a significantly better average score (946) compared to the initial 500-game run (400).

passages.heading: Chat with the trained model
passages.text: The first three replies are what the corpus taught. The fourth is a negation failure. The model drew white, the color the story rejected, but for this exact prompt the probes in [results/expanded/probes.json](results/expanded/probes.json) put black first at 0.479 and white at 0.085, so the reply was an unlikely draw at temperature 0.8. The fifth is the limitation the assignment asks to show. The question's words are mostly outside the vocabulary, the model receives them as unknown tokens, and it replies with `the team discussed the car was`, pieces of a classroom frame and a negation story with no meaning together, because continuing text is the only thing it does and it has no idea of a question. The notebook's own chat cell, section 10, produced one more turn from the same model during Run All, `the customer` followed by `returned the item after checking the price .`, saved in [results/expanded/chat_transcript.json](results/expanded/chat_transcript.json).

passages.text:
- In scope: ingest a small set of sources, maintain a clear index, retrieve relevant notes, cite them.
- Out of scope: autonomous edits, multi-agent coordination, public deployment, and broad web search.

**Tip**

The boundary is the point. A retrieval system you fully understand beats an agent you can’t debug. The optional v2 (next class) and v3 (Class 7) builds earn the tools and then the team — while the graded capstone, Assignment 5, applies the same discipline to a 10,000-record insight pipeline.

passages.heading: Summary
passages.text: This note details the "Networking Tracker" web app built for Assignment 1 of Fundamentals of Agentic AI. The app functions as a private contact list for Berkeley connections, enforcing data privacy using Postgres Row Level Security. The technology stack includes Next.js on Vercel, Neon Postgres, Neon's managed Better Auth, and the Neon Data API.
